name: supercut-to-youtube

deploy.description: Supercut Recordings row's YouTube Status set to Ready for YouTube (Notion database automation -> catch hook) -> Supercut transcript -> AI by Zapier writes title, description, tags and chapters, and checks for client names against the company-ID Table -> Supercut render + signed download URL -> YouTube Upload Video, unlisted -> YouTube Video ID, URL and status written back. YouTube Status set to Public -> videos.update makes it public. TKT-1069. Source of truth: https://github.com/work-flowers/zapier-sdk/tree/main/supercut-to-youtube

trigger.trigger_note: Catch hook. A Notion database automation on Supercut Recordings (When YouTube Status is set to Ready for YouTube or Public -> Send webhook) POSTs { source, data: <page> } to webhook_url. The automation must be created by hand in Notion after the first publish; until then nothing fires.

connections_note: supercut is an API by Zapier connection holding Dennis's personal Supercut token (sk_u_..., the one the supercut-sync worker uses); /download needs a personal token. youtube is the workFlowers channel (UCbrz9V64Z2x5OBveDo5ee4w), the default YouTube connection since 2026-11-20. AI by Zapier and Zapier Tables need no connection.

notion.note: Supercut Recordings is managed by the supercut-sync Notion Worker. The five YouTube properties were added by hand on 2026-11-20 and are not declared by the worker, so they stay writable. No create_database_item call here, so repo rule 5 does not apply.

tables.01JM8PH8YM93A482M8BFZ6WKW6: Company IDs Table. Rows with a Harvest Client ID (258 on 2026-11-20) are the client list the AI step checks transcripts against. Read only, free.

ai_model.why: Metadata writing plus a client-mention check over a short transcript; no tool calls. TKT-1069 said Claude, and Dennis chose the repo default on 2026-11-20. Verified 2026-11-20 on seven real recordings (README table): all six already-uploaded demos produced usable metadata and no false client flags, and the Knoxx demo was flagged.
